Subject: NovaHealth – identity & operational assurance checklist

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As part of our procurement and security review we need a concise checklist of how Redwood supports our identity controls (SSO, SCIM, RBAC, admin separation) plus any operational evidence you can share. The questionnaire in the attachment is long, but at minimum we need:
- SAML/OIDC support and metadata exchange process
- SCIM provisioning scope and attribute mappings
- RBAC model and admin role separation (can you do delegated admins per tenant?)
- Audit logging, retention windows, and access to logs
- Any shared responsibility notes around customer-managed keys and VPC/private deployment

Can you respond with a single consolidated thread and attach any artifacts (config snippets, SCIM sample map, SAML metadata) we can pass to our security team?

Claire
Security Operations
NovaHealth

Attachment: novahealth_iam_questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: NovaHealth – identity & operational assurance checklist

Claire,

Appreciate the clear list — I’ve summarized answers below and attached a short evidence bundle and SCIM attribute map. Neha (solutions) is looped in for technical details; Marissa (CS) will cover operational runbook/SLAs if we proceed.

High-level answers (see attachments for examples):
1) SAML & OIDC: Redwood supports both provider-initiated and SP-initiated SAML 2.0 flows and OIDC (authorization code + PKCE). We provide SAML metadata (attached) and a one-click OIDC client config file. IdP certificate rotation is supported via metadata exchange; we provide a validation workflow for thumbprints.

2) SCIM provisioning: Full SCIM 2.0 support for users and groups. We support bulk imports, incremental sync with ETag handling, and attribute mapping via a CSV (attached). SCIM operations are authenticated with OAuth2 bearer tokens scoped per tenant.

3) RBAC & admin roles: Multi-tenant RBAC with fixed built-in roles (Account Admin, Org Admin, Billing Admin, Read-Only) and custom role creation. Delegated admin: yes — you can scope admins to an org/tenant and prevent cross-tenant elevation. Policy enforcement is server-side and audited.

4) Audit & logs: All admin actions and token issuance events are logged and retained for 13 months in hosted plans (configurable on Dedicated/Private deployments). Logs are exportable to your SIEM via secure syslog or forwarder (we included sample forwarding config).

5) Keys & network: For Private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations; for VPC deployments the control plane is customer-isolated. Hosted customers may use Redwood-managed keys by default; we can offer customer-managed keys for enterprise contracts.

Attachments: redwood_iam_evidence_v1.zip (contains sample SAML metadata, SCIM map, audit-sample.log), scim_attribute_map.csv, saml-metadata.xml

Next step: Neha, can you add the SCIM attribute mapping notes and a short paragraph about session/idle controls?

Thanks,
Ben
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: NovaHealth – identity & operational assurance checklist

Claire — following up with the technical specifics you asked for. I’ve kept this succinct; happy to jump on a call to walk through config.

SAML/OIDC specifics:
- SAML: Support for SHA-256 signatures; we accept entityID + ACS/assertion consumer URL in metadata. We enforce audience and recipient checks and validate InResponseTo when present. Metadata exchange: we’ll provide our SP metadata and accept either a metadata URL or static upload; certificate rotation is handled via metadata refresh and a brief validation window to avoid downtime.
- OIDC: Authorization Code + PKCE for web/native apps; we support standard claims and allow custom claims mapping into tokens. Token introspection endpoint is available for enterprise tenants.

SCIM provisioning details:
- Endpoint: /scim/v2/Users and /scim/v2/Groups, TLS 1.2+ required.
- Auth: OAuth2 client credentials scoped to provisioning.
- Rate limiting: 120 req/min per tenant (burstable with Dedicated plans).
- Conflicts: We surface 409 responses with server-side merge hints; we support bulk PATCH operations for group membership adjustments.
- Attribute map: recommended primary identifier is externalId mapped to user.external_id; we included a CSV sample showing attribute mappings and examples for email, givenName, familyName, and metadata fields.

RBAC and delegated admin:
- Built-in roles + custom roles with permission granularity at the API surface (generate_tokens, manage_users, manage_infrastructure, view_billing).
- Delegated admin: scopeable via org_id and resource tags. A delegated admin cannot modify another org’s settings unless explicitly granted cross-org scope. We also support time-limited admin elevation for emergency access with approval logging.

Session and controls:
- Idle session timeout configurable per tenant (default 30m for hosted).
- JWT refresh tokens can be configured with rotation.
- Admin console session MFA required for Account Admin role (we recommend enforcement for all admin roles).

Audit & retention specifics:
- Events captured: user lifecycle, role changes, token grants, SCIM bulk operations, model-deploy/reversion events tied to identity changes.
- Retention: 13 months standard, options to extend to multi-year on Dedicated/Private with S3/GCS export.
- Access: logs are accessible via console, API, and SIEM forwarders. We can provide a daily digest to security@novahealth.com.

If helpful I can produce a short runbook showing the SCIM onboarding steps and a sample SAML metadata exchange flow.

Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Identity
Redwood Inference

Thanks Neha — that level of detail is exactly what our SOC/InfoSec team needs. A couple quick follow-ups from security:
1) Can you confirm whether SCIM provisioned accounts can be soft-deleted (flagged) vs hard-delete? We need a recoverable option for 90 days.
2) For delegated admin, how are emergency elevations approved and audited? We’d like an approval chain (two approvers) and timeboxed elevation.
3) Are session termination hooks available so we can force logout for a user from our SIEM incident response?

Also, we’ll want a short architecture diagram for the SCIM flow and a sample syslog forwarder config for ingestion into Splunk. Can you commit those artifacts by EOD Friday?

Claire

Claire — quick answers inline and noted artifacts at the bottom.

1) Soft-delete: Yes. SCIM deletes are implemented as a "soft-delete" flag at the tenant level by default. Accounts are recoverable for 90 days; during that window provisioning clients receive a 200 OK with a status change and a deleted timestamp. We can optionally expose a hard-delete API restricted to Account Admins if you require it.

2) Emergency elevation: We offer an "expiring elevation" flow where an admin requests elevation via the console or API which triggers a two-approver workflow by default (configurable). The elevation is timeboxed (default 1 hour) and all approvals, approver identities, and justification are recorded in the audit log. Elevations can be revoked and the revoke is also logged.

3) Session termination hooks: Yes — we expose a revocation endpoint and an admin action that forces logout. For automated response we provide a webhook that can be triggered by your SIEM which will call our revocation endpoint; we included a sample webhook + syslog forwarder snippet in the evidence bundle.

Artifacts committed:
- SCIM onboarding diagram (drive link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/SCIM_ONBOARD_DIAG)
- Splunk syslog forwarder example (file: splunk_syslog_forwarder.conf)
- Short runbook for SCIM onboarding (file: scim_onboarding_runbook.md)

If you want, Jonas can run a quick call next week to demo the onboarding runbook end-to-end.

Neha Kapoor
